sources.entry: UBOS - Linux distro that runs on indie boxes (personal servers and IoT devices). Single-command installation and management of apps - Jenkins, Mediawiki, Owncloud, WordPress, etc., and other features. GPL-3.0 Perl

summary.name: UBOS
summary.one_liner: UBOS is an open-source project for running self-hosted web applications on user-controlled servers, built around a curated Arch Linux distribution called UBOS Linux.
use_cases: run a personal server at home
install self-hosted web apps like WordPress or MediaWiki
manage server-side web applications on own hardware
build social web applications with graph middleware
deploy apps on indie boxes or IoT devices
summary.what_it_does: The page lists four parts of the UBOS project. UBOS Apps are applications that can be managed with UBOS Gears. UBOS Gears are tools to deploy and manage server-side web applications on user-controlled servers, described as production-ready for physical and virtual machines. UBOS Linux is a curated subset of Arch Linux that supports UBOS Gears, listed as production on x86_64 and ARM. UBOS PeerGraph is graph-based middleware for building social web applications and is still under development.
notable: Linux distribution curated from Arch Linux for running web apps on personal servers
UBOS Gears manages server-side web apps on user-controlled hardware
UBOS PeerGraph is graph-based middleware for social web apps (under development)
Listed on awesome-selfhosted; licensed GPL-3.0 and written in Perl per listing
caveats: UBOS PeerGraph is still under development
